items.title: Should You Buy Qualcomm Stock For The Cash As Apple Leaves?
items.summary: Qualcomm (QCOM) throws off free cash worth 5.2% of its market value each year, against 4.4% for the median S&P 500 company. A yield above the median means one of two things: a bargain or a business the market expects to shrink. Here it is mostly the second: the cash comes from smartphone chips, and Apple is leaving.

items.title: What Does AT&T Stock Do To Your Money When The Market Falls?
items.summary: AT&T (T) is up 4.4% over the last five trading days, while the S&P 500 is down 1.1%. Strength in a weak tape pulls money in. That five-day move is not the question. The question is what holding AT&T does to your money when the market moves, because over the past year it has tended to go the other way.

items.title: Is PepsiCo Stock Cheap Enough To Live With Slow Growth?
items.summary: PepsiCo (PEP) has gone nowhere for a year, down 1.8% over the past twelve months while the S&P 500 returned 16.6%. At about $135 a share it trades at 17.7 times earnings, against an S&P 500 median of 22.5. A big cash generator priced below the market is what value buyers hunt for, so is this discount impatience or a verdict.

items.title: CME Group Rises 5.8% in a Year: How Should You Play the Stock?
items.summary: CME is expanding through higher trading volumes, new derivatives products and record market-data revenues while returning capital to shareholders.

items.title: Recurring Revenues Aid SPGI Despite Investment Pressuring Margins
items.summary: S&P Global's recurring revenues, AI adoption and productivity gains support growth as rising investment costs and a business reset pressure margins.

items.title: Should Record Revenue Make IonQ Stock Feel Safer?
items.summary: IonQ (IONQ) stock trades at about $37, roughly 55% below its high inside the last year. The market did not do that: over the past twelve months the S&P 500 returned 16.6% while IonQ lost 33.4%. Its own numbers went the other way, which makes the downside hard to size.

items.title: 3 Stocks With Below-Average Yields and Above-Average Dividend Growth. Why That Trade-Off Wins Long Term
items.summary: Chasing the biggest dividend yields can quietly sabotage long-term income, and three mega-cap businesses with some of the smallest payouts on the market reveal exactly why the math works against most income investors.

items.title: Utility costs could put pressure on cities’ finances, S&P experts warn
items.summary: S&P Global analysts see a “simmering risk” from high electricity and water costs but momentum in affordable housing and sustainable debt.
